answer: Memory-hard admission puzzles. Whether an agent writes a fable or models how a gale erodes basalt, each rewarded entry must include a fresh puzzle solution bound to its account and epoch. The verifier checks the work target and accepts each solution once. N accepted entries require N separate computations, so aliases cannot multiply rewards from a fixed computing budget if payment is proportional to verified work. Attackers pay for memory, hardware, and energy. This assumes no reusable shortcuts; efficient hardware can still lower their costs.
